title: Presentable cartesian monoidal localization of the Joyal model
statement:
Use simplicial sets, universes, quasicategories and coherent functors of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Joyal model structure and categorical equivalences $W$ of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and the cartesian pushout-product property of [lem-coef-joyal-cartesian-pushout-product]. Combinatorial means locally presentable with set-generated weak factorization systems, as in [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]; tractable means combinatorial with a set of generating cofibrations whose sources are cofibrant. Left proper means that a pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence.

The Joyal model category is left proper, combinatorial and tractable, and its underlying category is cartesian closed. Every simplicial set is cofibrant. Its homotopy coherent localization $q:N(\mathsf{sSet})\to\mathsf{sSet}[W^{-1}]_\infty$ is saturated: a strict simplicial map $f$ belongs to $W$ if and only if $q(f)$ is an equivalence. With its monoidal localization, this localization is equivalent as a symmetric monoidal infinity category to the cartesian monoidal infinity category $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ of small quasicategories of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure]. In particular $q$ is a strong symmetric monoidal functor on all simplicial sets, including the terminal unit: there are coherent equivalences $q(K\times L)\simeq qK\times qL$ and $q(\Delta^0)\simeq\mathbf1$. These assertions hold in each universe and after enlarging the ambient universe.
